::: {.callout-note}
This is a living essay under active development. Its central artifact is a controlled comparison using the same base model, data split, and evaluation harness.
:::

> **Thesis.** Post-training is a sequence of distribution-shaping problems: supervised imitation, preference estimation, constrained policy optimization, and evaluation under imperfect rewards.

## What the reader will build

- A QLoRA supervised fine-tuning baseline
- A pairwise preference dataset and reward model
- A miniature PPO/RLHF loop with explicit KL control
- DPO implemented directly from its loss equation
- A small GRPO experiment on verifiable tasks
- A unified evaluation report and model card

## Chapter 1 · From a base model to an assistant

### History and theory
<!-- Base → continued pre-training → SFT → preference/RL → safety and evaluation. -->

### Mathematics
<!-- Token cross-entropy, prompt masking, packing, and mixture weighting. -->

### Colab implementation
<!-- QLoRA SFT with explicit chat templates, masks, checkpoints, and tests. -->

### Ablation and visualization
<!-- Data amount, epochs, learning rate, rank, and prompt-token masking. -->

### Failure analysis
<!-- Overfitting, catastrophic forgetting, format learning, and misleading demos. -->

## Chapter 2 · Preference data and reward models

### History and theory
<!-- Chosen/rejected data, rubrics, position/style bias, and process supervision. -->

### Mathematics
<!-- Bradley–Terry probability, pairwise logistic loss, margin, and calibration. -->

### Colab implementation
<!-- Construct preference pairs and train a small reward model or reranker. -->

### Ablation and visualization
<!-- Label noise, length bias, imbalance, reward distributions, calibration curves. -->

## Chapter 3 · RLHF and PPO from first principles

### History and theory
<!-- Policy, reference, reward, and value models; rollout and optimization phases. -->

### Mathematics
<!-- Policy gradient, importance ratio, clipped objective, GAE, entropy, KL penalty. -->

### Colab implementation
<!-- Implement toy PPO, then reproduce the same training signals with TRL. -->

### Ablation and visualization
<!-- Clip range, KL coefficient, reward scale, entropy, and policy collapse. -->

## Chapter 4 · DPO and direct preference optimization

### History and theory
<!-- DPO assumptions and contrasts with PPO, IPO, ORPO, KTO, and SimPO. -->

### Derivation
<!-- Derive DPO from KL-regularized RL; explain beta, log-ratios, implicit rewards. -->

### Colab implementation
<!-- Write the DPO loss directly and match a library implementation numerically. -->

### Ablation and visualization
<!-- Beta, reference model, preference noise, response length, and difficulty. -->

## Chapter 5 · Reasoning RL and GRPO

### History and theory
<!-- Verifiable rewards, group sampling, process/outcome rewards, curricula, hacking. -->

### Mathematics
<!-- Group-relative advantages, normalized rewards, KL, and estimator variance. -->

### Colab implementation
<!-- Implement mini-GRPO on a verifiable task and preserve all sampled rollouts. -->

### Ablation and visualization
<!-- Group size, temperature, KL, reward shaping, output length, correctness. -->

## Chapter 6 · Evaluation, safety, and research judgment

### Evaluation system
<!-- Offline/online eval, LLM judges, human agreement, contamination, confidence intervals. -->

### Safety and red-teaming
<!-- Refusal, over-refusal, jailbreaks, capability–safety trade-offs, data flywheels. -->

### Unified comparison
<!-- Compare base, SFT, reward model, DPO, PPO, and GRPO under one protocol. -->

### Model card and research proposals
<!-- Intended use, limitations, risks, failure taxonomy, and three follow-up experiments. -->

## Reproducibility checklist

- [ ] All checkpoints share the same documented base model
- [ ] Train and evaluation data are separated and decontaminated
- [ ] Preference formatting and chat templates are identical across methods
- [ ] Reward, KL, entropy, length, and task metrics are logged together
- [ ] Ablations change one primary variable at a time
- [ ] Failed or unstable runs are included
- [ ] Safety and capability regressions are both reported
- [ ] The model card distinguishes evidence from speculation
